intro.title: Build role based access middleware
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a role-based access middleware function for a Node.js application. This middleware will check a user's role from a request and allow or deny access to specific routes. You'll learn how to use Express middleware, conditional logic, and HTTP status codes to enforce access control. The main technologies involved are Node.js, Express, and JavaScript functions. By the end, you'll have a reusable middleware that can protect routes based on user roles.
intro.usecase: Role-based access control (RBAC) middleware is a fundamental pattern in any multi-user application where permissions differ by user type. For example, in a SaaS dashboard, an admin might see user management panels and billing settings, while a regular user only sees their own profile and usage data. This middleware ensures that API endpoints or UI routes are protected, preventing unauthorized access to sensitive operations like deleting records or viewing financial reports. As a Node.js developer, you'll implement this to secure backend services for e-commerce platforms, internal admin tools, or collaborative apps, where defining clear access boundaries is critical for security and user experience.
